en: Petavatthu,
Ubbarivagga,
11. Suttapetavatthu
“In the past, having approached a monk who had gone forth,
I requested and gave him a discourse;
the ripening of that deed is now obtained as a vast fruit.”
And many millions of garments appeared for me.
My delightful celestial mansion was strewn with flowers,
variegated, and frequented by men and women.
I eat and I clothe myself,
and yet my abundant wealth does not diminish;
this is due to the following ripening of that very same karma.
"Both happiness and pleasure are found here;
having gone back once more to the human world,
O son of a noble man, I shall perform meritorious deeds."
“You have come here seven hundred years ago;
there you will become worn out and aged.
All those kinsmen of yours have already passed away.”
"What will you do there after going from here?
"Seven years have passed since I arrived here,
fully endowed with celestial bliss."
"Having gone back once more to the human world,
O noble son, I shall perform meritorious deeds.
Having seized her by the arm with force, he—
Having brought back the very frail elder nun, he dismissed any other person who had come there, saying:
"Perform meritorious deeds; happiness is easily obtained."
I have seen how both ghosts and likewise humans are tormented by their own unwholesome deeds; yet,
having performed actions that lead to pleasant results, [they rejoice].
“Both gods and humans are beings established in happiness.
Thus ends the eleventh *Sutta-petavatthu*.
